focus: Inbound email with unusual subjects — very long, empty, contains newlines
summary: Found 1 HIGH and 1 MED issue. The HIGH is that the custom_channel_message validator on :subject (added by this feature) blocks candidate-sent inbound emails if the subject contains {{placeholder}} text — the email is silently dropped. The MED is that inbound email subjects containing newlines are stored as-is without sanitization, which is a defense-in-depth concern for email header injection when the subject is later used in outbound Mailgun calls.

findings.detail: The line `validates :subject, custom_channel_message: true` (added by this feature, commit e7f272279) applies the CustomChannelMessageValidator to the subject field. This validator rejects any value matching /{\{\s*[\w.]+\s*\}}/i. When a candidate replies via email and their subject contains text like '{{JobTitle}}' or '{{anything}}', the ChannelMessage fails validation. Channel#send_message_to_company calls `save` (line 45 of channel.rb) which returns false, but EmailProcessor (line 78) does not check the return value. The candidate's reply is silently dropped — no error logged, no notification sent, no retry. The candidate believes their reply was delivered; the hiring team never sees it.
findings.reproducer: Build a ChannelMessage with sent_by: 'sent_by_candidate', subject: 'Re: {{JobTitle}} Application', body: 'Normal text'. Call save. Returns false with error: 'Subject Message not sent. An invalid placeholder formatted like {{Something}} was found.'
findings.suggested_fix: Add `unless: :sent_by_candidate?` to the subject validation (and ideally the body validation too, since the same pre-existing bug exists there): `validates :subject, custom_channel_message: true, unless: :sent_by_candidate?`
findings.notes: The body validation had the same pre-existing bug (blocking candidate messages with {{}} in body), but the subject validation was added by this feature commit. Both should be fixed.

findings.detail: Pre-existing bug widened by this feature: `validates :body, custom_channel_message: true` blocks candidate-sent inbound emails if the body contains {{placeholder}} text. Before this feature, the validator was named custom_channel_message_body but had the same logic and the same bug. This feature renamed it to custom_channel_message (same code) and applied it to both :body and :subject. The body bug is pre-existing but was never scoped to non-candidate messages. Since the feature touched this exact line (renamed the validator), it's in-scope for this review.
findings.reproducer: Build a ChannelMessage with sent_by: 'sent_by_candidate', body: 'Hi, I noticed {{CandidateName}} in your template', subject: 'Re: Job'. Call save. Returns false.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `unless: :sent_by_candidate?` to the body validation: `validates :body, custom_channel_message: true, unless: :sent_by_candidate?`
findings.notes: This exact bug existed before the feature but the feature commit touched the line (renamed validator). The fix is trivial and should be applied alongside F1.

findings.detail: The clean_incoming_message callback (before_create) cleans the body but does NOT clean/sanitize the subject. A subject containing newline characters (\n, \r\n, \r) is stored as-is in the database. When the subject is later used in ChannelMessageMailer#notify_candidate (line 116), it is passed directly to Mailgun as the Subject header value. Newlines in email headers can cause header injection attacks (injecting additional headers like Bcc:). While Mailgun likely sanitizes on their end, defense-in-depth says the app should strip newlines from subjects before storage. Verified: stored bytes [72, 101, 108, 108, 111, 10, 87, 111, 114, 108, 100, 13, 10, 84, 101, 115, 116, 13, 83, 117, 98, 106, 101, 99, 116] — all newline variants preserved.
findings.reproducer: Build a ChannelMessage with subject: "Hello\nWorld\r\nTest\rSubject". Save succeeds. Reload and check subject.bytes — newlines are preserved.
findings.suggested_fix: In clean_incoming_message, add: `self.subject = subject&.gsub(/[\r\n]+/, ' ')&.strip` to sanitize newlines from subjects.
findings.notes: This is a new attack surface introduced by the subject field. The API controller path (channel_messages_controller.rb line 37) sanitizes subject via Rails sanitize(), but the inbound email path does not sanitize subjects at all.

findings.detail: PostgreSQL 'character varying' (no limit) stores the full 300-char subject without truncation or error. Input length 300, stored length 300. No data loss risk from long subjects.

Empty string subject saved OK. Mailer fallback in notify_candidate (line 116) uses subject.presence which returns nil for empty string, so the fallback 'Software Engineer at Acme Inc.' is used. SendTemplateEmail#add_subject would not raise because the fallback is non-blank.
nil subject saved OK (column is null: true). Mailer fallback works correctly.
Deeply nested 'Re: Re: Re: ...' subject (216 chars, 50 levels deep) saved and retrieved correctly. No truncation or error. Email clients handle nested Re: natively.
